clue.text: Sun lovers do this second-rate quiz

parts.note: B grade is second-rate, below A
to quiz someone is to ask them questions

explanation.surface: A sunbathers' quiz that isn't up to much.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying in warm sunshine and enjoying it is the classic sunbathers' pastime.

clue.text: Cheese contains bug, climbing metal vessel

indicators.note: the cheese word holds the other pieces within its letters

parts.note: Brie is a soft French cheese

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means the word is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: to bug someone is to nag them
tin is a metallic element

explanation.surface: A cheese with an insect crawling up it, next to some metal container.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reverses the bug word, as a down clue reads upwards. 'vessel' looks like a container, but it is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A two-masted sailing ship of a type once favoured by pirates.

clue.text: Rock star rakes it in somewhat, being top of the charts?

indicators.note: takes, with in, says the singer's name swallows the next word
with takes, signals that one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: Sting is the rock singer formerly of The Police
taken as written
pretty, as in pretty good, means somewhat

explanation.surface: A rock star earns a bit by reaching number one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes ... in' puts the pronoun inside the singer's name. The definition is figurative: a chart-topper is comfortably placed.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a comfortable, advantageous position, as anyone at number one is.

clue.text: Gross director, in Swindon complex, rules tyrannically

parts.note: gr is the abbreviation for gross (144)

indicators.note: the director letter is placed within the rearranged town name
complex means complicated, so the town's letters are jumbled

parts.note: a town in Wiltshire, England

explanation.surface: An unpleasant film director working at a Swindon complex lords it over everyone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' jumbles SWINDON into INSDOWN; D goes in after the N. Swindon is an English town.
explanation.definitionFit: To oppress or crush people by harsh, unrelenting domination.

clue.text: Carnival site embraces old German and italian landmark

indicators.note: the city name wraps around the German word

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is famed for its carnival
alt is German for old

explanation.surface: A carnival city hugs an elderly German and an Italian monument.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'old German' is the German word for old, not a person.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rialto is the famous bridge (and district) on Venice's Grand Canal.

clue.text: "On return, a good rule is to avoid Abergavenny," spluttered old Welshman

indicators.note: spluttered words come out jumbled, so the town's letters are mixed

parts.note: a market town in Monmouthshire, Wales

indicators.note: the small pieces are read backwards, though as letters to drop their order does not matter

parts.note: R stands for rule, as in rex or regulation

explanation.surface: Someone on the way home declares a golden rule: stay away from Abergavenny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is to avoid' removes A, G and R from ABERGAVENNY; 'spluttered' mixes the rest, BEEVANNY, into the politician's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Aneurin Bevan, Welsh Labour politician who founded the National Health Service.

clue.text: Foreign convoy resort to damage in Diana's company abroad

parts.note: a spa is a health resort

indicators.note: the damage word sits within the rearranged name
the name's letters are sent away and travel abroad, signalling a rearrangement

parts.note: to harm is to damage

explanation.surface: A foreign fleet heads to a resort to wreak havoc while Diana is overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'company abroad' jumbles the name to NISADA, and 'in' puts the damage word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The fleet Philip II of Spain sent against England in 1588.

clue.text: No cash machine? Alex abruptly changed colour

parts.note: O, a zero, means none
an ATM is an automated teller machine

indicators.note: changed means altered, so the shortened name is rearranged
something cut off abruptly loses its end, here the final letter

explanation.surface: Alex, finding no cash machine, suddenly went pale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abruptly' cuts ALEX to ALE; 'changed' turns it into EAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A pale greyish-beige shade named after ground oats.

clue.text: One close to computer in lair, withdrawn?

definitions.text: One close to computer in lair, withdrawn?

indicators.note: the final letter is placed inside the reversed hideout
withdrawn means pulled back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair

indicators.note: close to means the end, so the last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A reclusive geek hunched over a computer in their den.
explanation.walkthrough: DEN reversed is NED; R, the last letter of computer, goes inside. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsessive, socially awkward enthusiast, often of computing.

clue.text: Knit, ignoring husband, during the excellent broadcast

parts.note: in means during, as in in the night

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered, so the letters are rearranged
ignoring means leaving out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: great means excellent

explanation.surface: Knitting during a great television programme, leaving the husband out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignoring' drops H from THE; 'broadcast' mixes TE plus GREAT into TEGRATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to join closely together, combining parts into a whole.

clue.text: Love public attention in serving up egg flip

indicators.note: the three pieces are placed within the reversed egg word
in a down clue, serving up means delivering upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
love is zero in tennis, O
overt means open, public
heed means attention, as in pay heed

explanation.surface: A chef who loves the limelight serves an egg flip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving up' reverses the egg word, giving GGE. 'Egg flip' looks like a drink, but 'flip' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To flip is to lose one's temper or sanity, losing control completely.

clue.text: Cruise, perhaps westwards, tarot card revealed

indicators.note: in an across clue, westwards means right to left, so the letters run backwards
revealed means shown, the letters being visible within the words

explanation.surface: Tom Cruise flips a tarot card westward to reveal his fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Reading 'tarot card' backwards gives DRACTORAT, where the answer sits.
explanation.definitionFit: Tom Cruise is an example of a film performer.

clue.text: A paramour teased hedonist during a meal

indicators.note: the jumbled word sits within the meal phrase

parts.note: a bite is a snack or small meal

indicators.note: teased means combed out or pulled apart, signalling rearrangement

explanation.surface: A lover mocks a pleasure-seeker over dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teased' rearranges the pleasure-seeker to ONTHESID; 'during' puts that inside the meal, before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret lover outside a marriage or main relationship.

clue.text: Sit angrily, preparing complaint

indicators.note: preparing means making ready, so the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone sits sulking while getting ready to grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' looks like a grievance but is used in the medical sense, an ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: Inflammation of the voice box, an ailment that makes one hoarse.

clue.text: Playful dog, say, heads for green grass trespassing true to form

indicators.note: the initials trespass, i.e. intrude into, the rearranged word
to form means to be shaped, so the letters are rearranged
heads means the first letters of the next words

explanation.surface: A frisky dog runs onto the lawn, behaving true to type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to form' rearranges the word true to TUER, and 'trespassing' puts the two initials inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog that likes to pull at toys in a tug-of-war game is one that tugs.

clue.text: Paradise for reflection, everyone starts to appreciate household toilet

indicators.note: reflection as in a mirror flips the whole string backwards

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: starts means first letters of the following words

parts.note: lav is short for lavatory

explanation.surface: A heavenly retreat for contemplation where all value the family bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: ALL+AH+LAV is ALLAHLAV; 'for reflection' reverses the whole string.
explanation.definitionFit: In Norse myth, the hall where slain warriors feast with Odin, an afterlife heaven.

clue.text: Newshound's latest sleazy tale in type — from this source?

definitions.text: Newshound's latest sleazy tale in type — from this source?

indicators.note: the letters go inside the type word

parts.note: ilk means type or kind

indicators.note: latest means the last letter is taken
sleazy suggests something corrupted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tabloid reporter's sordid story, perhaps born of gossip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sleazy' rearranges the tale to LETA; 'in' puts it, with D from 'latest', into the type word. The whole clue suggests gossip as a reporter's source.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip and chatter, the kind of loose talk a reporter might mine.

clue.text: Badly-done fencing brought back domestic parasite?

indicators.note: fencing means enclosing, so the rearranged word surrounds the other
badly means poorly made, so the letters are rearranged
brought back means reversed

parts.note: a domestic animal is tame

explanation.surface: A shoddy garden fence lets a household pest in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Badly' rearranges the participle to NODE; 'brought back' gives EMAT; 'fencing' puts EMAT inside NODE. 'domestic' suggests a house, but means tame.
explanation.definitionFit: A roundworm, many of which live as parasites in animals and plants.

clue.text: Scorpion initially attacks group of animals — most stingy

parts.note: Scorpion is this puzzle's setter, who refers to himself as me

indicators.note: initially means the first letter

parts.note: a nest can mean a brood or group of animals

explanation.surface: A scorpion strikes a group of creatures with its sting.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters often refer to themselves by pseudonym; here 'Scorpion' is the setter, ME.
explanation.definitionFit: Most stingy is most tight-fisted, a superlative of miserly.

clue.text: See 2 Down
College threesome

explanation.surface: A college with three members.
explanation.definitionFit: Trinity is a college at Cambridge, Oxford and Dublin; a trinity is also a group of three.

clue.text: Seen around front of ruins, like some churches

indicators.note: the seen word wraps around the letter

parts.note: spied means seen

indicators.note: front means the first letter

explanation.surface: Spotted near the ruins, like some old churches.
explanation.walkthrough: R, the first letter of 'ruins', goes inside SPIED.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a tall pointed steeple, as many church towers do.

clue.text: Fair competition given examination by court?

parts.note: A level is the British advanced-level school examination
a court for sport is a playing area

explanation.surface: A fair contest held at a court examination.
explanation.walkthrough: A levels are the British exams taken at about 18.
explanation.definitionFit: An equal footing where nobody has an advantage, an idiom for fairness.

clue.text: Hairstyle for a vagrant

indicators.note: vagrant means wandering, so the letters wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A drifter's particular haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A rounded, bushy natural hairstyle.

clue.text: See 22
A building site includes hideaway for retiring circus performer

indicators.note: the rearranged word holds the reversed word inside it
building means constructing, so the letters are put together anew
retiring means withdrawing, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a lair is a hideaway

explanation.surface: A building site contains a retreat for a shy circus performer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'building' rearranges site to EIST; 'retiring' gives RIAL, which 'includes' places inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze or tightrope artist who performs high up.

clue.text: Honest mistakes by children in trouble

indicators.note: mistakes means errors, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: kids are children

explanation.surface: Honest children's errors get them into bother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakes' looks like a noun but is the anagram signal, making ONTHES from HONEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading for failure or ruin, an idiom for being in a declining state.

clue.text: Batsman's opening OK, making contribution to total?

indicators.note: opening means the first letter

parts.note: yes means okay

explanation.surface: A batsman's first run is acceptable towards the score.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, byes are runs scored without the batsman hitting the ball, added as extras to the team's total.
explanation.definitionFit: Byes are extras, runs added to a cricket score without the bat touching the ball.
